eligibility_reason: Nimbus Textiles is a growing, profitable business but carries elevated leverage (3.81x Debt/EBITDA), near-maxed WC limits (96.3% utilised), 4 cheque bounces, thin liquidity (0.09 months cash cover), a material cash/bank-statement reconciliation break, and ambiguous receivables data — approval is viable only with strict haircuts, escrow, concentration covenants, and resolution of all data-quality flags as conditions precedent.

recommended_products.purpose: Unlock cash trapped in trade receivables to relieve the near-fully-drawn CC/WCDL limits without adding EMI-bearing term debt; self-liquidating from debtor collections
recommended_products.amount_basis: Step 1 — Use LOWER/more conservative eligible-receivable base: Dataroom 0-60d = INR 49,161,370 vs MIS 0-60d (28,524,448 + 25,006,135) = INR 53,530,583; conservative = INR 49,161,370. Step 2 — Apply 80% base advance rate (standard 70-85%). Step 3 — Top customer (Vastra Global Exports) outstanding INR 35,092,141 = 71% of total receivables; apply 25% concentration haircut on Vastra-linked receivables. Vastra eligible share (pro-rata 0-60d): 49,161,370 × 40.3% = INR 19,812,032; haircut to 60% advance = INR 11,887,219. Non-Vastra eligible: 49,161,370 − 19,812,032 = INR 29,349,338 at 80% = INR 23,479,470. Total eligible pool = 11,887,219 + 23,479,470 = INR 35,366,689. Step 4 — Round down conservatively to INR 24,500,000 (~69% of pool) to stay within a prudent first-draw limit given data-quality ambiguity on ageing.
recommended_products.repayment: self-liquidating — each invoice discounted repaid on collection from named debtor within 30-90 day cycle; revolving within sanctioned limit
security: Escrow/collection account: all debtor payments routed through lender-controlled escrow; surplus released to Nimbus after repayment of each discounted invoice
Personal guarantees of Mahesh Patel (55%) and Bhavna Patel (30%)
Negative lien on existing fixed assets (pari passu with Bank of Baroda)
covenants: Eligible receivables (0-60d) to be refreshed monthly; limit auto-reduces if eligible pool falls below INR 30,625,000 (1.25x cover on INR 24,500,000)
Single-debtor concentration cap: no more than 50% of outstanding discounted invoices from any one debtor
90+ day receivables not to exceed 15% of total book (currently 20% on dataroom; 13.9% on MIS — trigger at 15% requires immediate ageing reconciliation)
Vastra Global Exports LLP invoices: advance rate capped at 60%; maximum exposure INR 12,000,000
Cheque/payment return events: any further bounce triggers 48-hour cure notice; two bounces in any rolling 6-month period triggers facility review
Monthly MIS submission within 15 days of month-end (debtor ageing, collections, utilisation)
conditions_precedent: Resolution of data-quality flag 'mis_vs_dataroom_ageing': borrower to provide auditor-certified debtor ageing as at a single cut-off date reconciling MIS (INR 87,626,053) vs dataroom (INR 75,632,877); limit sized off whichever is lower

Resolution of data-quality flag 'bs_cash_vs_bank_statement': CA-certified explanation of INR 35,856,898 gap between balance-sheet cash (INR 2,600,000) and bank-statement closing (INR 38,456,898); if unexplained, treat balance-sheet figure as operative
Resolution of data-quality flag 'cashflow_reconciliation_break': restatement of Mar-26 cash-flow statement to eliminate INR 36,173,218 forced closing
Submission of all three sanction letters (Bank of Baroda TL, Tata Capital WCDL) to confirm outstanding balances and security positions
Execution of escrow/collection account agreement with named debtors' acknowledgement of assignment
KYC and credit check on Vastra Global Exports LLP (export debtor, 40.3% concentration) — minimum acceptable: no NPA/default history
Updated GST returns (Apr-25 to Mar-26) reconciled to revenue of INR 321,000,000
monitoring: Monthly debtor ageing statement (auditor/CA certified, within 15 days of month-end)
Escrow account daily balance feed to lender
Quarterly financials with DSCR and leverage recomputation
Alert if Vastra Global Exports outstanding exceeds INR 12,000,000 or payment overdue >60 days
Annual limit review tied to audited financials
Cheque/ECS return tracker — immediate notification to lender on any return
serviceability_check: Existing annual debt service: TL EMI INR 820,000/month × 12 = INR 9,840,000 principal; interest on CC INR 67,500,000 × 10.6% = INR 7,155,000; interest on WCDL INR 24,000,000 × 12.0% = INR 2,880,000; interest on TL INR 21,000,000 × 11.2% = INR 2,352,000; total existing debt service ≈ INR 22,227,000 (matches snapshot annual_debt_service_inr)
Invoice discounting is SELF-LIQUIDATING — no new EMI or fixed principal obligation added to DSCR denominator; interest cost on INR 24,500,000 at 9.9% = INR 2,425,500/year (incremental interest only)
Revised annual debt service = INR 22,227,000 + INR 2,425,500 = INR 24,652,500

DSCR marginally below 1.25x covenant norm — however, invoice discounting replaces drawn CC/WCDL utilisation (not additive net debt); if INR 24,500,000 of CC/WCDL is repaid from ID proceeds, interest saving = INR 24,500,000 × ~11% blended = INR 2,695,000/year
Net revised debt service (ID replaces CC/WCDL draw) = INR 22,227,000 − INR 2,695,000 + INR 2,425,500 = INR 21,957,500
Net post-facility DSCR = INR 29,532,000 / INR 21,957,500 = 1.345x — ABOVE 1.25x threshold; structure is serviceable on a net-replacement basis
Condition: lender to confirm INR 24,500,000 ID proceeds are used to repay CC/WCDL drawdown (end-use covenant); DSCR covenant set at >= 1.25x tested quarterly

recommended_products.product: Cash Credit (CC) — Restructuring / Rationalisation of Existing Bank of Baroda CC
recommended_products.purpose: Rationalise the existing near-maxed CC limit (96.4% utilised, INR 67,500,000 outstanding vs INR 70,000,000 sanctioned) by introducing a drawing-power discipline linked to eligible receivables and inventory, reducing effective limit to a serviceable level; not a new facility but a restructured renewal with tighter controls
recommended_products.amount_basis: Step 1 — Drawing power formula: eligible receivables (0-60d, conservative) INR 49,161,370 × 75% = INR 36,871,028; plus eligible inventory (inventory INR 50,076,000 × 50% standard textile haircut) = INR 25,038,000; gross DP = INR 61,909,028. Step 2 — Apply 10% overall haircut for data-quality flags (ageing ambiguity, cash reconciliation break) = INR 55,718,125. Step 3 — Round down to INR 55,000,000. Step 4 — This is INR 15,000,000 BELOW current sanctioned limit of INR 70,000,000, requiring INR 12,500,000 repayment of current outstanding (INR 67,500,000 → INR 55,000,000) funded from ID proceeds above.
recommended_products.repayment: revolving — repaid from collections; annual renewal subject to audited financials and DP recomputation
security: First charge hypothecation of current assets (inventory + receivables) — existing Bank of Baroda charge to be confirmed and updated
Second charge on fixed assets (net block INR 49,400,000)
Personal guarantees of Mahesh Patel and Bhavna Patel
Drawing power to be recomputed monthly from CA-certified stock and debtor statements
covenants: Drawing power recomputed monthly; outstanding not to exceed DP at any time
Current Ratio >= 1.20 (currently 1.13 — borrower to improve within 2 quarters via ID-funded CC repayment)
Debt/EBITDA <= 3.5x (currently 3.81x — to be achieved within FY2026-27 as TL amortises)
DSCR >= 1.25x tested semi-annually on trailing 12-month EBITDA
90+ day receivables <= 15% of total book; breach triggers DP reduction by equivalent amount
No incremental borrowing from any lender without prior written consent
Cheque return limit: maximum 2 returns in any rolling 12-month period; breach triggers cash collateral of 10% of limit (INR 5,500,000)
conditions_precedent: Repayment of INR 12,500,000 from CC outstanding (from ID proceeds) before revised limit is operative
Submission of all sanction letters (data-quality flag: sanction_letter_partial_coverage) — Bank of Baroda TL and Tata Capital WCDL sanction letters to be provided
Reconciliation of balance-sheet cash vs bank-statement closing (data-quality flag: bs_cash_vs_bank_statement) — CA certificate required
Reconciliation of MIS vs dataroom debtor ageing (data-quality flag: mis_vs_dataroom_ageing)
Updated stock statement and debtor statement as at restructuring date
Confirmation from Bank of Baroda of existing charge details and no cross-default clauses triggered by limit reduction
monitoring: Monthly stock and debtor statements (within 10 days of month-end) for DP recomputation
Quarterly financials with covenant compliance certificate
Annual audited financials within 180 days of fiscal year-end
Immediate notification of any cheque/ECS return
serviceability_check: CC is revolving — no fixed principal repayment; interest cost on revised limit INR 55,000,000 at 10.5% = INR 5,775,000/year
Existing CC interest (INR 67,500,000 × 10.6%) = INR 7,155,000; saving from limit reduction = INR 1,380,000/year
Revised total debt service: TL EMI INR 9,840,000 + CC interest INR 5,775,000 + WCDL interest INR 2,880,000 + TL interest INR 2,352,000 = INR 20,847,000
Post-restructuring DSCR (before ID) = INR 29,532,000 / INR 20,847,000 = 1.416x — comfortably above 1.25x
Conclusion: CC restructuring to INR 55,000,000 improves DSCR headroom and brings leverage closer to 3.5x target as TL amortises

declined_products.product: Fresh Term Loan (new capex or balance-sheet TL)
declined_products.reason: Debt/EBITDA already 3.81x (above 3.0x norm); current ratio 1.13 (below 1.2 covenant); 4 cheque bounces; thin liquidity (0.09 months cash cover); adding fixed EMI obligations would push DSCR below 1.25x. No capex need identified in snapshot.

declined_products.product: Incremental Working Capital Demand Loan (new WCDL)
declined_products.reason: Existing WCDL (Tata Capital) already 96% utilised at INR 24,000,000; total WC limits 96.3% drawn; adding another WCDL increases leverage beyond 3.81x Debt/EBITDA and worsens current ratio (already 1.13); repayment source is the same constrained operating cash flow.

Governance flag (pledging_disclosed = null), 4 cheque bounces, unresolved cash reconciliation break of INR 35,856,898, and ambiguous ageing data make unsecured exposure inappropriate at this credit quality.

key_risks: Customer concentration (Vastra Global Exports 40.3% of revenue, INR 35,092,141 outstanding): mitigated by capping Vastra-linked invoice discounting at INR 12,000,000 (60% advance rate) and requiring KYC/credit check on Vastra as a CP

Data integrity — three material reconciliation breaks (cash gap INR 35,856,898, ageing gap INR 11,993,176, cashflow forced closing INR 36,173,218): mitigated by making CA-certified reconciliation of all three a hard condition precedent before any disbursement

Near-maxed WC limits (96.3% utilised) and thin liquidity (0.09 months cover): mitigated by replacing CC draw with self-liquidating ID proceeds, reducing CC limit to INR 55,000,000 with DP discipline, and routing collections through escrow
Cheque bounces (4 in 12 months): mitigated by cash-collateral trigger (10% of CC limit) on any further bounce, and ID escrow ensuring collections bypass borrower's operating account

Elevated 90+ day receivables (20% on dataroom, 13.9% on MIS — ambiguous): mitigated by using lower/conservative dataroom base for eligible receivable sizing, and a 15% 90+ day covenant with auto DP reduction on breach

Leverage above norm (3.81x Debt/EBITDA vs 3.0x guideline): mitigated by declining new term debt, reducing CC limit, and setting a Debt/EBITDA covenant of 3.5x with a glide path as the existing TL amortises (INR 820,000/month)
rationale: Lead product is Invoice Discounting, not a new CC/TL, because WC limits are 96.3% drawn and adding EMI debt risks DSCR below 1.25x — ID is self-liquidating.
Conservative eligible-receivable base of INR 49,161,370 used (dataroom 0-60d, lower than MIS INR 53,530,583) per data-quality flag 'mis_vs_dataroom_ageing'.
Vastra Global Exports (40.3% revenue, INR 35,092,141 outstanding) triggers concentration haircut: advance rate cut to 60% and exposure capped at INR 12,000,000.
INR 35,856,898 cash/bank-statement gap (flag 'bs_cash_vs_bank_statement') is unresolved; balance-sheet cash of INR 2,600,000 used as operative figure — confirms 0.09 months liquidity cover.
CC restructured down from INR 70,000,000 to INR 55,000,000 (DP-linked); INR 12,500,000 repayment funded from ID proceeds improves current ratio toward 1.20 covenant.
Post-restructuring DSCR = INR 29,532,000 / INR 20,847,000 = 1.416x; net ID-replacement DSCR = 1.345x — both above 1.25x floor.
Debt/EBITDA at 3.81x exceeds 3.0x norm; no new term debt recommended; covenant set at 3.5x with natural deleveraging as TL (INR 820,000/month EMI) amortises over 48 months.
4 cheque bounces in 12 months (high severity) addressed via cash-collateral trigger (10% of CC = INR 5,500,000) and escrow routing of ID collections.
Sanction letter covers only 1 of 3 facilities (flag 'sanction_letter_partial_coverage'); submission of all three sanction letters is a hard CP before any new disbursement.
FY2025-26 figures used throughout (latest year); revenue INR 321,000,000, EBITDA INR 29,532,000, PAT INR 7,139,660 — all show consistent 8-10% growth trajectory supporting conditional approval.
